title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: section 5 of the notes on the stratification at infinity of \bar M_{g,ν}. An 'MD-graphe' (Mumford–Deligne graph) is the stable dual graph of a stable marked curve. Grothendieck encodes a graph as (S, Ã, σ_Ã, o: Ã→S): S is the set of vertices, Ã the set of half-edges ('arcs'), σ a fixed-point-free involution pairing half-edges into edges, and o the origin map. The extra data are a genus function γ: S→N and a map I→S distributing the marked points over the vertices. The previous page gave the formulas (4_0) for the 'specialised' graph G' obtained by inserting a graph G(α) at each vertex α of G. This page spells out, for a fixed vertex α of type (g_α, Î_α), what the insertion datum is. Here Î_α = I_α ⊔ Ã_α, where Ã_α is the set of half-edges of G with origin α.
(1) A connected graph (S(α), Ã(α), σ, o).
(2) A genus map γ_α: S(α)→N.
(3) A map I_α→S(α), which distributes the marked points lying over α among the new vertices.
(4) A map Ã_α→S(α), which gives each half-edge of G at α a new origin vertex β.
(5) Stability: every genus-0 vertex β must have at least 3 special points (marked points plus half-edges).
Implicitly, by the 'type numérique' of the previous page, the genus of G(α) must equal g_α, i.e. Σ_β γ_α(β) + b_1(G(α)) = g_α. The resulting G' (vertices ⊔S(α), half-edges Ã ⊔ ⊔Ã(α)) is an MD-graph related to G by specialisation: G' is the more degenerate graph, and G is recovered by contracting the edges inside each G(α). Grothendieck then announces a digression on morphisms of graphs, the 'morphismes de généralisation' G'→G, together with the functoriality of the fundamental groupoid π_1(G). This is the standard description of the face relation among boundary strata of \bar M_{g,n}: the closure of the stratum of G contains the strata of all G' obtained by inserting stable graphs at the vertices, equivalently G' → G contracts a set of edges.
errors: The genus constraint g(G(α)) = Σ_β γ_α(β) + b_1(G(α)) = g_α is not restated among conditions 1°)–5°); it is only implicit in the 'type numérique (g_α, ν̂_α)' of the previous page.

The stability condition card I_{α,β} + card Ã_{α,β} ≥ 3 must count all half-edges at β: the internal ones from Ã(α) (loops counted twice) as well as the external ones from Ã_α. As written, Ã_{α,β} could be read as only the external arcs; presumably Î_{α,β} including internal half-edges is meant.

The phrase 'G' qui se spécialise dans G' has ambiguous direction. G' is the more degenerate graph: its stratum lies in the closure of G's stratum, and the map G'→G is a contraction ('morphisme de généralisation').

ideas.what: Combinatorial encoding of graphs via half-edges with an involution and an origin map, decorated by a genus function and marked legs
ideas.modern_name: Stable graphs / dual graphs of stable curves (half-edge formalism)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kontsevich, Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998), Manin; dual graphs going back to Deligne–Mumford and Knudsen
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the 'structure à l'infini' / Mumford–Deligne stratification informally

ideas.what: Insertion of stable graphs at the vertices of a stable graph, yielding a more degenerate stable graph; stability condition ≥3 at genus-0 vertices
ideas.modern_name: Graph insertion / composition in the modular operad of stable graphs; edge-contraction morphisms of stable graphs; face relation of boundary strata of \bar M_{g,n}

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but standard setup of graph insertion for stable dual graphs, i.e. the specialisation/contraction relation of boundary strata. It is an early, explicit half-edge formulation anticipating modular-operad language, but it contains nothing beyond what is now textbook.
transcription_corrections: Item 5°): 'définissent une {+o-connexe [?], G(α)+} marquette [?]' likely reads 'définissent un {connexe, G(α)} graphe marqué' or similar (an insertion 'connexe' above the line); 'marquette' is probably a misreading.
Item 1°) correctly includes the inserted word 'connexe' above 'graphe'; the struck symbol is a deleted A(α).
